summary: Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1962–1968), where he later held posts, before holding the chair for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Gendun Lodro studied under Khensur Ngawang Legden and completed his ge-shay degree at Drepung Monastery by 1961. He held positions at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1992) and as resident teacher at the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Karma Sonam held posts at Gyume Tantric Monastery (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held posts at Tibet House (1986–1989), the University of British Columbia (2002), and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

Geshe Lhundub Sopa was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who earned his Lharampa Geshe at Sera Monastery (1941–1962) under teachers including Geshe Lhundrub Thabkhe. He served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 to 1997.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lobsang Tharchin studied at Gyume Tantric Monastery and earned his Lharampa Geshe degree at Sera Monastery by 1953.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics, both attested in 2010.

A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Lozang Jamspal studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His appointments include the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Delhi, and the Columbia University faculty (attested 1985–1990).

Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and Trijang Rinpoche. He served at Leiden University (1960) and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery. A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–2019) and held visiting posts at Smith College (2004).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Palden Drakpa served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (attested 1987–1992, 2004) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Geshe Rabten studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, earning his Geshe Lharampa degree (~1940–1959). He later taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. In 1978, he became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Tashi Tsering studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries, as well as under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1990–1992) and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Tenzin Dhargye studied at Sera and Gyume Tantric Monasteries and under Ling Rinpoche. He held posts at Gyume, the University of Virginia (1999–2000), and became director at Tibet Center Austria in 2008.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Yeshe Tobden studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Lodrö Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He spent his career at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925), succeeding Bunyiu Nanjio.
